environment.description: Same content management server behind CloudFront distribution (ID: E2XYZABC123) with Origin Access Control (OAC) configured using signing protocol SigV4. The origin (ALB) has security group sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f that restricts inbound HTTPS to CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing). CloudFront distribution has a custom origin request policy that strips non-allowlisted headers. The batch input files are sourced from an S3 bucket (content-queue-prod) with a bucket policy requiring aws:SecureTransport and restricting PutObject to role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ContentIngestionRole which has a permissions boundary (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:policy/IngestionBoundary) limiting s3:PutObject object keys to pattern 'batches/*.tsv' with a maximum object size of 1024 bytes enforced via s3:content-length-range condition. The ingestion Lambda that writes to the queue bucket performs NFC normalization and rejects any line where the post-NFKC-normalized filename differs from the pre-normalized version by more than case folding, effectively collapsing the unicode attack surface before the CLI tool ever sees it.

config.origin_security_group: sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f, inbound only from CloudFront prefix list
config.s3_bucket_policy: PutObject restricted to ContentIngestionRole with permissions boundary
config.ingestion_lambda: Pre-normalizes input with NFKC, rejects lines where normalization changes path semantics
config.signed_urls: CloudFront signed URLs with 300s TTL, key group KG-PROD-2024
